title: Article 97 — Salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker

content.overview: Article 97 provides that there shall be paid to the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and to the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People, such salaries and allowances as may be respectively fixed by Parliament by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries and allowances as are specified in the Second Schedule.
content.glance: Salaries/allowances of RS Chairman & Deputy Chairman and LS Speaker & Deputy Speaker: fixed by Parliament by law; until then, Second Schedule.
content.study:
Article 97 authorises Parliament to fix salaries and allowances of the four parliamentary officers (RS Chairman/Deputy Chairman; LS Speaker/Deputy Speaker). Pending such law, the Second Schedule applies.

Examination: parliamentary power to fix; Second Schedule as interim.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Salaries and allowances of Chairman, Deputy Chairman, Speaker and Deputy Speaker are fixed by Parliament by law; until then, as in the Second Schedule.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How are the salaries of the Speaker and Chairman fixed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 97, the salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States and of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People are such as may be fixed by Parliament by law, and until so fixed, as specified in the Second Schedule.

examTips: Parliament by law; interim Second Schedule.

keyTakeaways: Art 97: salaries of parliamentary officers fixed by Parliament; interim Second Schedule.
